annotation_description: Playing Flooded Strand turn 1 wastes the fetchland's landfall trigger. If cracked immediately to get an Island and cast a crab, the crab isn't on the battlefield when the Island enters, so no mill occurs. The fetchland's double-landfall potential (fetch entering + fetched land entering) is wasted without a crab in play.

Fetching basic Island instead of Watery Grave delays the ability to cast Glimpse the Unthinkable. With Watery Grave (untapped, paying 2 life) plus Cephalid Coliseum as the turn 2 land drop, the player could cast Glimpse the Unthinkable on turn 2. With basic Island, there's no black source available in hand besides Undercity Sewers (not in hand) - the player would need to draw into a black source to cast Glimpse.

Declined to activate Mishra's Bauble, missing a free peek at opponent's top card and a card draw next upkeep. While keeping an artifact on board helps with Kappa Cannoneer's Improvise and future Construct tokens from Urza's Saga, the card advantage from Bauble activation is typically more valuable, especially since the player needs to find lands/spells to develop their game plan.
Playing Polluted Delta before casting Hedron Crab means the Delta entering only triggers Ruin Crab (mill 3) instead of both crabs (mill 6). This costs 3 cards of mill.

Cracking Polluted Delta while the second Ruin Crab is still on the stack means only 1 Ruin Crab triggers from the land entering. By waiting for Ruin Crab #2 to resolve and casting Hedron Crab first, the Delta crack would trigger all 3 crabs (2 Ruin Crabs + Hedron Crab) for 9 mill instead of 3, losing 6 cards of mill. Additionally, playing Cephalid Coliseum after all crabs are in play would maximize further triggers.

message: Select an Island or Swamp card
annotation_description: Fetched a basic Island when the player has Glimpse the Unthinkable (UB) in hand and no black mana sources on the battlefield. Fetching Watery Grave (paying 2 life to enter untapped) would have enabled casting Glimpse the Unthinkable this turn alongside playing Cephalid Coliseum or another land, providing a huge mill tempo advantage. A basic Swamp would also have been better to enable Glimpse next turn without life loss.

Playing Urza's Saga as the land drop triggers all three of opponent's crabs (2 Ruin Crab + 1 Hedron Crab) to mill 9 cards total, directly fueling the opponent's mill gameplan. Against a dedicated mill deck, unnecessary land drops that trigger landfall are very costly.

Casting a second Mox Opal from hand when one is already on the battlefield is problematic due to the legend rule. The player will have to sacrifice one of the two Mox Opals immediately. While this does trigger Weapons Manufacturing (creating another Munitions token) and the legend rule sacrifice could feed Arcbound Ravager if it were on the battlefield, the Ravager is in the graveyard. The player is essentially spending a card from hand just to get a Munitions token and a Weapons Manufacturing trigger. However, casting Emry first would have been better sequencing - Emry has affinity for artifacts and already costs very little with the artifacts in play, and Emry could then tap to recur an artifact from the graveyard (like Arcbound Ravager or Lavaspur Boots). The Mox Opal play does create value through Weapons Manufacturing, but losing a card permanently for just a Munitions token when Emry could provide recurring value seems suboptimal.

Against a dedicated mill deck with Ruin Crabs and Hedron Crab, casting Emry mills 4 additional cards from your own library, actively advancing the opponent's win condition. With already 10 cards in graveyard, this accelerates the clock significantly.

Field of Ruin is significantly better here than Watery Grave. The opponent has two Urza's Sagas on the battlefield, which are extremely dangerous enchantment lands that will create large Construct tokens and tutor for artifacts. Field of Ruin can destroy one of them. More importantly, when Field of Ruin is activated, both players search their libraries, which enables Archive Trap to be cast for free (0 mana) to mill 13 cards. The player has Archive Trap in hand, so playing Field of Ruin sets up a devastating sequence: activate Field of Ruin to destroy an Urza's Saga, trigger the library search, then cast Archive Trap for free, all while triggering the three crabs from both the Field of Ruin land drop AND the basic land entering from Field of Ruin's effect (two landfall triggers). Watery Grave tapped provides mana fixing but no immediate impact and misses the Field of Ruin + Archive Trap synergy.

With Emry untapped and a graveyard full of powerful artifacts (Shadowspear, Arcbound Ravager, Mishra's Bauble, Lavaspur Boots), the player should be activating Emry to target an artifact to cast this turn. Against mill crabs that are rapidly depleting the library, tempo is critical and every resource should be utilized. Tapping Emry for Shadowspear or Arcbound Ravager would significantly advance the board state.

Archive Trap is on the stack about to mill 13 cards. With 24 cards already in the graveyard, the player is in serious danger of being decked. The opponent's entire strategy is mill, and letting a free 13-card mill resolve when you have a counter available is potentially game-losing.

Cephalid Coliseum taps for U but deals 1 damage to self, and its threshold ability requires 7+ cards in graveyard (Coach only has 3). Field of Ruin produces colorless but can destroy opponent's Urza's Saga and when activated later, both players searching for basics triggers additional landfall mill from the crabs. Both lands enable Glimpse the Unthinkable this turn.

Failed to activate Mishra's Bauble for free card advantage. With the player's library being heavily milled by opponent's crabs, every card draw matters. Mishra's Bauble activation is essentially free - it draws a card next upkeep and provides information. Emry can also recast it from the graveyard later if needed. Metalcraft would still be active (4 artifacts remaining).
